name: Roti (whole wheat), 2 per serving

steps.text: Knead 200 g atta with the oil, salt and about 120 to 130 ml warm water into a soft dough, pressing and folding for 5 minutes.
steps.cue: The dough is smooth and soft and springs back slowly when pressed, without sticking to your hand.
steps.tip: Add water a tablespoon at a time. A dough that is too wet takes too much dry atta when rolling and the rotis turn tough.

steps.text: Cover the dough with a damp cloth and rest it for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Resting relaxes the gluten, so the rotis roll out thin without shrinking back.

steps.text: Divide into 8 equal balls. Dust each ball lightly in atta and roll it into a thin circle about 15 cm across, turning it a quarter turn after each roll.
steps.cue: The circle is an even thickness with no thick centre or torn edges.

steps.text: Heat a tava over medium-high heat. Cook a roti for about 30 seconds until bubbles form, flip and cook 30 to 40 seconds until brown spots show, then flip again and press the edges lightly with a folded cloth, or hold it over a flame for a few seconds, until it puffs.
steps.cue: The roti puffs into a ball and has light brown spots on both sides.
steps.tip: The tava is hot enough when a drop of water dances and disappears within 2 seconds.

steps.text: Stack the cooked rotis in a clean cloth or a lidded container so the steam keeps them soft.
steps.cue: After 5 minutes in the cloth the rotis feel soft and bend without cracking.

storage: Wrap in a clean cloth for up to 2 days at room temperature, or refrigerate for 4 days. Reheat on a hot tava for 20 seconds a side. Raw dough keeps 2 days in the fridge.
